[[Perth]], Western Australia | key_people = {{ubl|Liz Westcott (Acting [[CEO]])|[[Richard Goyder]] ([[Chairperson|Chair]])}} | industry = [[Oil and gas industry|Oil and gas]] | products = {{ubl|[[Petroleum]]|[[LNG]]}} | production = {{cvt|193.9|MMoilbbl}} of [[oil equivalent]] | production_year = 2024 | revenue = US$13.18 billion | revenue_year = 2024 | net_income = US$3.57 billion | net_income_year = 2024 | num_employees = 4,718 | num_employees_year = 2024 | website = {{URL|https://www.woodside.com/|woodside.com}} | footnotes = {{cite web |url=https://www.woodside.com/docs/default-source/investor-documents/major-reports-(static-pdfs)/2024-annual-report/annual-report-2024.pdf|title=Woodside Energy 2024 Annual Report|publisher=Woodside|access-date=27 March 2025}}{{Cite news |date=2025-12-17 |title=Meg O'Neill resigns as Woodside chief to join energy giant |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-12-18/meg-oneill-resigns-as-woodside-ceo-to-join-bp/106156568 |access-date=2025-12-20 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}} }} '''Woodside Energy Group Ltd''' (formerly Woodside Petroleum Ltd) is an Australian [[petroleum]] exploration and production company. Woodside is the operator of oil and [[LNG|gas]] production in Australia and also Australia's largest independent dedicated oil and gas company.{{cite web|url=https://www.woodside.com.au/about-us|title=Profile|website=Woodside Energy|access-date=29 September 2020}} It is a public company listed on the [[Australian Securities Exchange]] and has its headquarters in [[Perth]], Western Australia. In the 2025 [[Forbes Global 2000]], Woodside was ranked as the 494th-largest public company in the world.{{Cite web |title=Woodside Energy Group {{!}} Company Overview & News |url=https://www.forbes.com/companies/woodside-energy-group/ |access-date=2025-12-20 |website=Forbes |language=en}} ==History== Woodside was incorporated on 26 July 1954. It was originally established as Woodside (Lakes Entrance) Oil Co NL, a [[no liability company]] (NL), and named after the small town of [[Woodside, Victoria]].{{cite web|url=https://www.woodside.com.au|title=Home|website=Woodside Energy|access-date=10 April 2018}} The company was floated by accountant [[Rees Withers]], whose firm serviced a number of small exploration companies in [[Gippsland]] where Australia's first oil field had been discovered. The company initially struggled to raise funds after a lack of initial success.{{Cite news|url=https://adb.anu.edu.au/biography/withers-rees-bedford-30034|title=Withers, Rees Bedford (1913–1996)|first1=Robert|last1=Murray|first2=Kim|last2=McGrath|work=Australian Dictionary of Biography|year=2021}} In 1956, stockbroker Geoff Donaldson, who had underwritten the initial share offer, joined Woodside as chairman. He played a key role in keeping the company afloat in its early years.{{cite news|url=https://thewest.com.au/news/wa/woodside-founder-dies-aged-99-ng-ya-353170|title=Woodside founder dies aged 99|newspaper=The West Australian|date=3 July 2013|access-date=6 February 2023}} Woodside initially focused its exploration activities on Victoria's Gippsland Basin. In 1962 the company recruited [[Nicholas Boutakoff]] as chief geologist, who turned the company's activities towards Western Australia. He correctly hypothesised that the [[North West Shelf]] contained petroleum reserves, and in 1962 Woodside applied for exploration licences over a large offshore area. Woodside subsequently joined up with [[Shell Australia|Shell]] and [[Burmah Oil]] to form the original [[North West Shelf Venture]]. [[BHP]] later replaced Burmah, and with Shell, each became a 40% shareholder in Woodside in 1985.[https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/118197006 Shell will not support BHP] ''[[Canberra Times]]'' 10 April 1986 page 18 BHP reduced its shareholding to 10% in July 1990.[https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/120895225 BHP sells gas stake for $525m] ''Canberra Times'' 29 June 1990 page 13 In October 1994, BHP sold its remaining shares while Shell sold down to 34%.[https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/130534827 BHP, Shell in $501m sale of Woodside] ''Canberra Times'' 1 November 1994 page 17 In 1995, Woodside moved its head office from [[Melbourne]] to [[Perth]].[https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/133918300 Woodside to finally move west] ''Canberra Times'' 7 December 1995 page 17 In 1998, Woodside and the North West Shelf Joint Ventures executed a retrospective Indigenous Land Use Agreement for the North West Shelf Project area, which includes the Karratha Gas Plant on the Burrup Peninsula (Murujuga). This agreement is between the North West Shelf JV and the Ngarluma Yindjibarndi Foundation Ltd (NYFL). This is a non-royalty agreement{{Cite web |date=2019-12-10 |title=Woodside signs fresh Aboriginal deals |url=https://www.pilbaranews.com.au/news/pilbara-news/woodside-signs-fresh-aboriginal-deals-ng-b881400150z |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Pilbara News |language=en}}. Woodside is also a party to the Burrup and Maitland Industrial Estates Agreement (BMIEA) for operations areas including the Pluto Gas Plant{{Cite web |date=2019-09-19 |title=Burrup Native Title Agreement documents |url=https://www.wa.gov.au/government/publications/burrup-native-title-agreement-documents |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.wa.gov.au |language=en}}. The Traditional Owner parties to the BMIEA are represented by the Murujuga Aboriginal Corporation (MAC). In 2001 Shell sought to buy out the remaining portion of the company that it did not already own at the time; however, the takeover move was blocked by [[Treasurer of Australia]], [[Peter Costello]], on national interest grounds.{{cite news|title=Government rejects Shell bid for Woodside Petroleum|url=http://www.abc.net.au/pm/stories/s281616.htm|access-date=4 October 2013|newspaper=[[PM (Australian radio program)|PM]]|date=23 April 2001|author=Mark Willacy}} In November 2010, Shell reduced its 34% stake to 24%.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/dd5b9db2-eb68-11df-b482-00144feab49a|title=Shell reduces Woodside stake to fund projects|last=Pfeifer|first=Sylvia|date=8 November 2010|website=[[Financial Times]]|language=en-GB|url-access=subscription|access-date=10 April 2018}} In November 2017, Shell sold its remaining shares.[https://web.archive.org/web/20171116094803/https://www.shell.com/media/news-and-media-releases/2017/shell-further-reduces-its-interest-in-woodside.html Shell further reduces its interest in Woodside] [[Royal Dutch Shell]] 13 November 2017[https://web.archive.org/web/20171217185141/https://www.shell.com/media/news-and-media-releases/2017/shell-upsizes-sell-down-of-shares-in-woodside.html Shell upsizes sell down of shares in Woodside] Royal Dutch Shell 13 November 2017[https://www.reuters.com/article/us-shell-divestiture-woodside-idUSKBN1DD0XM Shell sells out of Woodside Petroleum for $2.7 billion] ''[[Reuters]]'' 13 November 2017 In August 2021, Woodside entered into an agreement with BHP to merge the latter's oil and gas assets with Woodside. The deal is subject to regulatory and shareholder approval[https://web.archive.org/web/20210818085100/https://www.bhp.com/media-and-insights/news-releases/2021/08/woodside-and-bhp-to-create-a-global-energy-company/ Woodside and BHP to create a global energy company] BHP 17 August 2021 and has been described by environmentalists as 'a disastrous outcome for Woodside shareholders and [the] climate'.{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-08-17/bhp-woodside-merger-oil-energy-company/100385084|title=BHP and Woodside combine businesses to form one of the world's biggest energy companies|date=17 August 2021|access-date=7 November 2021|website=Abc.net.au}} In May 2022, the merger with the BHP oil and gas assets was approved by approximately 98% of Woodside shareholders.{{cite web |last1=Rose |first1=Derek |title=Woodside shareholders back BHP oil merger |url=https://7news.com.au/business/energy/woodside-poised-for-41b-deal-with-bhp-c-6852709 |website=7 NEWS |access-date=4 June 2022 |language=en |date=18 May 2022}} As of June 2022, the merger was completed and the combined entity was listed on the [[New York Stock Exchange]] and the [[London Stock Exchange]].{{cite web |last1=Durrani |first1=Desiree |title=Woodside (ASX:WDS) acquires BHP Petroleum to create global energy company |url=https://themarketherald.com.au/woodside-asxwds-acquires-bhp-petroleum-to-create-global-energy-company-2022-06-01/ |website=The Market Herald |access-date=4 June 2022 |date=1 June 2022}} Woodside agreed to buy American natural gas company, [[Tellurian Inc.]], for a total enterprise value of US$1.2 billion in July 2024.{{Cite news |last1=Williams |first1=Curtis |last2=Ojha |first2=Ayushman |date=22 July 2024 |title=Australia's Woodside Energy to buy US LNG developer Tellurian for $1.2 billion |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/australias-woodside-energy-buy-us-based-tellurian-12-bln-2024-07-21/ |publisher=Reuters}} The following month, Woodside announced it would acquire a "blue ammonia" project in Texas from OCI Global for US$2.35 billion.{{Cite web |last1=Levingston |first1=Ivan |last2=Massoudi |first2=Arash |last3=McCormick |first3=Myles |date=2024-08-05 |title=Woodside to buy OCI Global's 'blue' ammonia project for $2.3bn |url=https://www.ft.com/content/f5c38b8f-574d-4a32-9511-8e8e355faec4 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-08-08 |website=Financial Times}} ==Business overview== Woodside has exploration, development and operating activities in Australia and a number of international regions including Canada, United States, [[Senegal]], [[South Korea]], [[New Zealand]], [[Myanmar]], [[Cameroon]], [[Gabon]], [[Morocco]] and [[Ireland]]. Within Australia Woodside operates or is developing a number of [[liquefied natural gas]] projects. The company also operates the Enfield, Vincent and Pyrenees oil fields offshore from [[Exmouth, Western Australia|Exmouth]] in Western Australia.{{cite web|title=Woodside's Global Interests|url=http://woodside.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=e173091996454727bb6e8ef4a8de5a59 |website=Woodside Petroleum|access-date=29 September 2020}} ===Scarborough project=== {{main|Scarborough gas field}} Scarborough is the name of the gas field, {{cvt|375|km}} off the [[Pilbara]] coast.{{cite web | last=Kurmelovs | first=Royce | title=Woodside BHP forge ahead on Scarborough gas project in WA | website=The Guardian | date=22 November 2021 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/nov/22/woodside-bhp-forge-ahead-on-scarborough-gas-project-in-wa | access-date=15 February 2022}}{{cite web | title=Scarborough | website=Woodside | date=1 October 2021 | url=https://www.woodside.com.au/what-we-do/australian-growth-projects/scarborough | access-date=15 February 2022}} The project includes a floating production unit, the drilling of 13 wells, and a {{cvt|adj=on|430|km}} pipeline to transport the gas to the onshore [[Pluto LNG]] processing facility near Karratha, which will be expanded. A [https://climateanalytics.org/publications/woodsides-scarborough-and-pluto-project-undermines-the-paris-agreement 2021 study found] estimated that the full Scarborough-Pluto project will emit almost 1.4 billion tonnes of [[greenhouse gas]]es over its lifetime.{{Cite web |title=Woodside's Scarborough and Pluto Project undermines the Paris… |url=https://climateanalytics.org/publications/woodsides-scarborough-and-pluto-project-undermines-the-paris-agreement |access-date=2024-10-27 |website=Climate Analytics |language=en}} That's over three times Australia's current annual emissions, and around 14 times WA's annual emissions. A climate attribution study in the peer-reviewed journal showed that the emissions from the Scarborough project are directly linked to a temperature rise, leading to heat waves causing 484 heatwave deaths{{Cite web |last=News |first=Latest |date=2025-10-14 |title=Scientists link emissions from Woodside's Scarborough gas project to hundreds of heat-related deaths |url=https://theabj.com.au/2025/10/15/scarborough-gas-emissions-heat-deaths-study/ |access-date=2025-10-15 |website=Australian Business Journal |language=en-US}}{{Cite journal |last=Abram |first=Nerilie J. |last2=Maher |first2=Nicola |last3=Perkins-Kirkpatrick |first3=Sarah |last4=Falster |first4=Georgina M. |last5=Hughes |first5=Terry P. |last6=Meissner |first6=Katrin J. |last7=Slater |first7=Louise J. |last8=King |first8=Andrew D. |last9=Pitman |first9=Andrew J. |last10=Moon |first10=Gillian |last11=Morgan |first11=Wesley |date=2025-10-13 |title=Quantifying the regional to global climate impacts of individual fossil fuel projects to inform decision-making |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s44168-025-00296-5 |journal=npj Climate Action |language=en |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=92 |doi=10.1038/s44168-025-00296-5 |issn=2731-9814|doi-access=free |hdl=1959.4/106496 |hdl-access=free }} in Europe alone.{{Cite news |last=Lu |first=Donna |last2=editor |first2=Donna Lu Assistant |last3=climate |last4=environment |last5=science |date=2025-10-13 |title=Emissions linked to Woodside's Scarborough gas project could lead to at least 480 deaths, research suggests |url=https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2025/oct/13/woodside-scarborough-gas-project-emissions-could-cause-heat-deaths |access-date=2025-10-15 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}} The emissions from the Scarborough project have been attributed to expose more than half a million people to unprecedented heat, and kill 16 million corals in each bleaching event. Production is expected to begin in 2026.{{update after|2026}} The project has received environmental approval. ===Sunrise LNG development=== The Greater Sunrise gas development lies in the [[Timor Sea]] north of Australia and includes the Sunrise and Troubadour fields, which were discovered in 1974. Greater Sunrise is located about {{convert|450|km}} north-west of Darwin and {{convert|150|km}} south-east of [[East Timor]]. Approximately 80% of the fields lie within Australian waters, with the remainder in jointly administered waters. The Greater Sunrise fields have a total contingent dry gas resource of {{convert|5.13|e12cuft|abbr=off}} and {{convert|225.9|e6oilbbl|e6m3|abbr=off}} of condensate. The Sunrise JV participants are Woodside (operator) (33.4%), [[ConocoPhillips]] (30%), Shell (26.6%) and [[Osaka Gas]] (10%).{{Cite web|url=http://www.woodside.com.au/Our-Business/Developing/Pages/Sunrise.aspx|title=Sunrise LNG|website=Woodside Petroleum|access-date=10 April 2018|archive-date=27 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170127233234/http://www.woodside.com.au/Our-Business/Developing/Pages/Sunrise.aspx|url-status=dead}} In April 2010 Shell's [[floating liquefied natural gas]] technology was selected by the Sunrise Joint Venture for developing the Greater Sunrise gas fields in the Timor Sea. The Woodside-operated JV is now seeking to engage regulators on the concept selection process.{{cite web|url=http://www.shell.com/home/content/media/news_and_media_releases/archive/2010/flng_technology_greater_sunrise_29042010.html|title=Shell floating LNG technology chosen by joint venture for Greater Sunrise project|date=29 April 2010|website=Shell|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110529042931/http://www.shell.com/home/content/media/news_and_media_releases/archive/2010/flng_technology_greater_sunrise_29042010.html|archive-date=29 May 2011|url-status=dead|access-date=10 June 2011}} ===Australia Oil=== Woodside owns and operates a number of oil developments off Western Australia, including the Ngujima-Yin FPSO, the Pyrenees FPSO, and the Okha FPSO.{{Cite web|url=https://www.woodside.com/what-we-do/operations/australia-oil|title=Australia Oil|website=Woodside Petroleum|access-date=6 October 2022}} ===Burrup Hub=== Woodside Energy Group also has Burrup Hub, the largest fossil fuel project currently proposed in Australia, involving the extraction of six untapped gas fields and the drilling of 84 wells off the Western Australian coast.{{Cite web |last=Ritchie |first=Nick |date=2022-06-21 |title=Deep Sea Disaster Report Greenpeace |url=https://www.greenpeace.org.au/wp/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Deep-Sea-Disaster-Report-Greenpeace.pdf |access-date=2022-07-28 |website=Greenpeace}} ==Criticism== The construction of the Woodside-operated North West Shelf project in the 1980s included the destruction of more than 5,000 sacred rock art sites.{{Cite web |last=corporateName=Commonwealth Parliament; address=Parliament House |first=Canberra |title=Chapter 6 |url=https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Committees/Senate/Environment_and_Communications/BurrupPeninusla/Report/c06 |access-date=2025-09-14 |website=www.aph.gov.au |language=en-AU}} Ngarda-ngarli, the Traditional Owners, were blocked from protecting sites at the North West Shelf site, and consent was never provided for the construction of the Gas Plant, as per letters and records from Traditional Owners and archaeologists.{{Cite web |last=Seccombe |first=Mike |date=2025-06-07 |title='Done and dusted': Inside Labor's North West Shelf gas approval |url=https://www.thesaturdaypaper.com.au/news/environment/2025/06/07/done-and-dusted-inside-labors-north-west-shelf-gas-approval |access-date=2025-09-14 |website=The Saturday Paper |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2025-09-12 |title=As it happened: the North West Shelf gets its extension |url=https://www.energynewsbulletin.net/operations/news-analysis/4519952/happened-north-west-shelf-extension |access-date=2025-09-14 |website=www.energynewsbulletin.net |language=en}} Letters from Traditional Owners in 2025 show consent was never provided, and had still not been obtained in 2025, despite Woodside publicly committing to the United Nations Declaration on the Right of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP).{{Cite web |title=First Nations cultural heritage and engagement |url=https://www.woodside.com/sustainability/social/first-nations-cultural-heritage-and-engagement |access-date=2025-09-14 |website=Woodside |language=en-AU}} The final commonwealth approval{{Cite web |last=Watt |first=Murray |date=12 September 2025 |title=Press Conference, Brisbane, 12 September 2025, MURRAY WATT, MINISTER FOR THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER |url=https://minister.dcceew.gov.au/watt/transcripts/press-conference-brisbane-0}} for the extension of the North West Shelf oil and gas project until 2070 was ironically provided the day prior to the 28th anniversary of the UN adopting UNDRIP.{{Cite web |date=2025-09-12 |title=Aboriginal leaders unite to push for real change on rights and justice {{!}} Australian Human Rights Commission |url=https://humanrights.gov.au/about/news/media-releases/aboriginal-leaders-unite-push-real-change-rights-and-justice |access-date=2025-09-14 |website=humanrights.gov.au |language=en}} This was despite Traditional Owners publicly stating they had not consented to the original construction nor the extension of the Gas Plant.{{Cite news |date=2025-06-19 |title=Traditional owners want to see federal minister visit Murujuga country |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-06-20/traditional-owners-urge-government-consults-north-west-shelf/105432418 |access-date=2025-09-14 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}} In February 2006, the Mauritanian military junta led by [[Colonel|Col.]] [[Ely Ould Mohamed Vall]] denounced amendments to an oil contract made by former President [[Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya]] with Woodside Petroleum. In 2004, Woodside had agreed to invest US$600 million in developing Mauritania's Chinguetti offshore oil project.{{Cite web |date=2003-12-17 |title=Woodside to increase interest in Mauritania |url=https://www.offshore-mag.com/business-briefs/company-news/article/16771031/woodside-to-increase-interest-in-mauritania |access-date=2023-10-22 |website=Offshore}}{{Cite web |date=2004-09-14 |title=Woodside continues Mauritania exploration |url=https://www.offshore-mag.com/home/article/16802033/woodside-continues-mauritania-exploration |access-date=2023-10-22 |website=Offshore}} The "controversial" amendments, which Mauritanian authorities declared had been signed "outside the legal framework of normal practice, to the great detriment of our country", could cost Mauritania up to US$200 million a year.{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/4684836.stm|title=Mauritania and firm row over oil|date=6 February 2006|access-date=10 April 2018|work=[[BBC News]]}}{{cite news|last=Olphand|first=Marie-Pierre|date=6 February 2006|title=Crise ouverte avec la compagnie pétrolière Woodside|language=fr|work=Radio France Internationale|url=http://www1.rfi.fr/actufr/articles/074/article_41704.asp|access-date=10 April 2018}} In June 2006, the [[Australian Federal Police]] were investigating Woodside for allegations of bribery and corruption in Mauritania.{{cite web |url=https://www.theage.com.au/business/police-start-woodside-probe-over-bribery-claim-20061013-ge3br8.html|title=Police start Woodside probe over bribery claim |website=The Sydney Morning Herald|first1=Kate |last1=Askew |first2=Violeta |last2=Ayala |date=13 October 2006 |access-date=29 September 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/business/slick-operator-20060603-gdnocc.html|title=Slick operator|date=3 June 2006|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|access-date=29 September 2020}} In 2006–2007, as part of the Pluto [[LNG]] project, Woodside faced opposition over plans to build an onshore processing plant on the [[Burrup Peninsula]] in [[Western Australia]], as the site is home to significant [[petroglyph]]s up to 30,000 years old.{{cite web |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2008-07-25/resources-boom-putting-aboriginal-rock-art-at-risk/452390|title=Resources boom 'putting Aboriginal rock art at risk'|website=ABC News Online|date=25 July 2008|access-date=29 September 2020}} It has been suggested that intense lobbying by Woodside Petroleum contributed to the coalition [[Howard government]]'s initial decision against [[emissions trading]] in August 2000.{{Cite book|title=High & Dry: John Howard, Climate Change and the Selling of Australia's Future|last=Pearse|first=Guy|publisher=[[Penguin Books]]|year=2007|isbn=9780670070633|location=Camberwell, Vic.|pages=75}} The company also opposed the [[Rudd Government (2007–2010)|Rudd Labor government]]'s [[Carbon Pollution Reduction Scheme]] in 2009.Macdonald-Smith A ''[https://www.enn.com/articles/39434-woodside-â€˜remains-dismayedâ€™-at-australia-carbon-plan- Woodside ‘Remains Dismayed’ at Australia Carbon Plan]'' Bloomberg Press, 10 March 2009 Woodside is among six companies accused of making deceptive public statements in an attempt to get free carbon permits. The [[Australian Conservation Foundation]] says the companies exaggerated in public, but told a different story to their shareholders and investors. In June 2009, the ACF lodged an official complaint[http://www.acfonline.org.au/uploads/res/ACF-Complaint-to-ACCC.pdf] {{dead link|date=November 2021}} with the Federal consumer affairs watchdog asking that the matter be investigated.{{Cite web|url=http://www.acfonline.org.au:80/articles/news.asp?news_id=2311|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090619073113/http://www.acfonline.org.au/articles/news.asp?news_id=2311|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 June 2009|title=Contradictory carbon claims - ACCC complaint|website=Australian Conservation Foundation|access-date=10 April 2018}} The [[Australian Competition & Consumer Commission]] took no action against the companies.Senate gives resources giants nod on ETS evidence, by Laura Tingle, [[Australian Financial Review]], 8 September 2009 In April 2011 Australia's [[Fair Work Ombudsman]] began an investigation into claims that foreign workers were underpaid on two North West Shelf oil rigs operated by Woodside Petroleum.{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/lateline/ombudsman-investigates-foreign-worker-exploitation/2697006|title=Ombudsman investigates foreign worker exploitation|last=Barlow|first=Karen|date=27 April 2011|website=ABC News|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation|access-date=29 September 2020}} In April 2013, the [[Federal Court of Australia|Federal Court]] in WA heard allegations that the workers were paid less than A$3 an hour to work on the oil rigs. Documents tendered to the court claimed that the four men worked as painters on Woodside rigs on the North West Shelf off northern WA from July 2009 until early 2011.{{Cite news|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2013-04-08/court-to-hear-oil-rig-workers-paid-$3-an-hour/4615036 |title=Court hears oil rig workers paid $3 an hour|last=Lannin|first=Sue|date=8 April 2013|work=ABC News|access-date=29 September 2020|language=en-AU}} In the corporation's annual offshore performance report, published in mid-2013, the failure of an oil mist detector at Woodside Petroleum's Vincent oilfield in Western Australia was caused by faulty wiring and inadequately designed equipment. The issue was identified during a visit by a third party at Woodside's largest single source of oil production.{{cite news|author=Paul Garvey|date=6 June 2013|title=Woodside pulled up after failing to note safety flaw|newspaper=[[The Australian]]|url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/business/mining-energy/woodside-pulled-up-after-failing-to-note-safety-flaw/news-story/7d5dc485862bba41a62718b8b1c2a090|url-access=subscription|access-date=6 June 2013}} In April 2016, Woodside concealed a {{convert|10500|L|USgal}} oil spill off the coast of Western Australia, which went on for two months without anyone from the company noticing. Woodside's responsibility only came to light after intense public pressure.{{Cite news|url=http://www.theguardian.com/environment/2017/may/18/australian-oil-well-leaked-into-ocean-for-months-but-incident-kept-secret|title=Australian oil well leaked into ocean for months – but spill kept secret|date=17 May 2017|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=7 November 2021}} In March 2019, Woodside led a lobbying effort to force the Western Australia EPA to abandon new guidelines to protect the climate. The Australian Centre for Corporate Responsibility described the affair as a ‘week of shame.’{{Cite web|url=https://medium.com/lobbywatch/a-week-of-shame-premier-mark-mcgowan-the-epa-wa-and-the-fossil-fuels-lobby-2548b951bf88|title=A week of shame: how the fossil fuels lobby runs Western Australia|website=Medium.com|date=4 April 2019|access-date=7 November 2021}} In mid-2020, Woodside tried to avoid decommissioning costs by convincing regulators that dumping all the equipment from its Echo-Yodel field, including 400 tonnes of plastic, under the pretence of the waste being an 'artificial reef'.{{Cite on behalf of the [[Australian Conservation Foundation]] (ACF) sought an injunction against Woodside's Scarborough gas project due to its potential climate impacts on the [[Great Barrier Reef]]. Pride protest === Woodside Energy's involvement in [[Pride parade|Pride]] events has been a subject of controversy within the [[LGBTQ|LGBTQ+]] community. In 2019, the company became a major sponsor of Perth's PrideFEST,{{Cite web |date=2019-11-04 |title=Woodside becomes major supporting sponsor of Perth PrideFest |url=https://www.energynewsbulletin.net/policy/news/1374948/woodside-major-sponsor-perth-pridefest |access-date=2024-10-13 |website=www.energynewsbulletin.net |language=en}} a decision that drew criticism from activists who argued that corporate sponsorship undermines the radical spirit of the Pride movement.{{Cite web |last=OUTinPerth |date=2020-11-28 |title=Rainbow Rebellion call on Pride WA to return to their protest roots |url=https://www.outinperth.com/rainbow-rebellion-call-on-pride-wa-to-return-to-their-protest-roots/ |access-date=2024-10-13 |website=OUTinPerth |language=en-AU}} The Rainbow Rebellion group staged a protest in Perth's city centre in 2019, criticising Pride WA for prioritising corporate partnerships over political activism. They argued that corporations like Woodside Energy were using Pride events to distract from their harmful environmental practices. The [[Western Australian Greens]] party has also expressed concerns about Woodside's involvement in Pride events.{{Cite web |last=OUTinPerth |date=2022-11-16 |title=The Greens call on Pride WA to sever ties with sponsor Woodside |url=https://www.outinperth.com/the-greens-call-on-pride-wa-to-sever-ties-with-sponsor-woodside/ |access-date=2024-10-13 |website=OUTinPerth |language=en-AU}} In a letter to Pride WA, party leader [[Brad Pettitt]] called on the organisation to reconsider its association with the fossil fuel company. extract: Woodside Energy Group Ltd (formerly Woodside Petroleum Ltd) is an Australian petroleum exploration and production company. Woodside is the operator of oil and gas production in Australia and also Australia's largest independent dedicated oil and gas company. It is a public company listed on the Australian Securities Exchange and has its headquarters in Perth, Western Australia. In the 2025 Forbes Global 2000, Woodside was ranked as the 494th-largest public company in the world.
